subject: Renewal structure — flexible tenor, sprint uptake & convertible annualization

Subject: Renewal structure — flexible tenor, sprint uptake & convertible annualization

Hi Kimberly,

Our renewal window for the platform is coming up (Aug 1). We'd like to explore a structure that gives us flexibility as our usage ramps through the product sprint this year. High level asks from BrightAnchor: 

- Ability to start with a 12–18 month staged ramp (lower token commitment first 2 quarters, then step up)
- Option to convert to a 24/36 month annualized term at a defined trigger (convertible annualization)
- Clear auto-renew optics (we want a 30–60 day notification window)
- Safety net for burst capacity during spikes (short-term burst credits or guaranteed burst lanes)

I've attached our latest SOW (BrightAnchor_SOW_v3.docx). Can your team put together 1–2 term structures and a sample amendment we can review? Happy to hop on a 30-min call next week — Tue/Wed mornings PST work best for me.

Thanks,
Alicia Ramos
Director, Platform Partnerships
BrightAnchor Inc.
Procurement: procurement@brightanchor.com

Subject: Re: Renewal structure — flexible tenor, sprint uptake & convertible annualization

Hi Alicia — great to hear from you and thanks for the SOW.

We can absolutely model a few options that match BrightAnchor's goals. I sketched three pragmatic structures below (we'll pipeline a formal amendment for each):

1) Convertible-on-trigger (recommended)
   - Initial 12-month "sprint" term with staged commitments: 30% year-one baseline, step to 65% in Q3–Q4, full target in year 2.
   - Conversion window: if usage >= 90% of committed tokens over two consecutive quarters, client can elect to convert remaining months to a 24- or 36-month annualized term at a pre-agreed rate.
   - Auto-renew: 45-day opt-out window; notifications at 90/60/45 days.
   - Burst safety net: pre-purchased burst credits + on-demand burst lanes with capped premium.

2) Staged multi-year (lower admin friction)
   - 24-month term with built-in step-ups at 6/12 months and quarterly true-ups.

3) Annualize-later (most flexible)
   - 12-month initial contract with an option to extend to 36 months at fixed pricing if certain adoption milestones met.

Action items I suggest:
- Finance/legal (cc'd) to quick-check convertibility language and any revenue recognition constraints.
- I'll prepare a draft amendment (Redwood_Amendment_Draft_v1.pdf) with the Convertible-on-trigger as the primary option + 24-month alternative.

Availability: Tue 5/25 9–11am PST or Wed 5/26 9–10am PST. Which works for you?

Best,
Kimberly Park

Rishi / Vivek — quick heads up on BrightAnchor renewal (BA-4392). Alicia asked for a convertible annualization path + burst safety net. Key questions for finance/legal: 

- Is a conversion clause (12 -> 24/36) we propose likely to create recognition complexity we need to flag?
- Any guardrails we should add to avoid material revenue deferral (e.g., minimum commit floor or capped conversions)?
- On pricing: they may ask for phased discounting tied to committed token %; what range should we offer (5–15%) for a convertible path?

I will send them the draft as discussed but want alignment before we commit to language.

Thanks — K.

Kimberly — thanks for the thoughtful options. A few counterpoints from procurement and our finance owner: 

- Term preference: we prefer a 36-month overall envelope if we can keep a lighter immediate commitment (12–18 month low baseline) and step-ups thereafter.
- Burst safety net: procurement likes the idea of pre-purchased burst credits but would also like an SLA-backed rapid-burst lane with a 30-minute failover for critical jobs (we can give a list of 3 workloads).
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups are a must — we need regular visibility for our internal forecasting.
- Billing/DocuSign: procurement prefers a single amendment + SOW + DocuSign flow; happy to review a draft amendment.

We can do Wed 5/26 9am PST for a 30-min call. I'll loop in our finance lead on that invite.

Onward — Alicia

Thanks Alicia — appreciate the clarity. Per our internal review we can propose the following hybrid that maps to BrightAnchor's ask while limiting accounting friction: 

Proposed commercial summary (final amendment to follow):
- Term: 30-month convertible envelope (initial 12-month low baseline + option to annualize remaining term to 24/36 at conversion trigger).
- Commit & step-up: baseline 35% of target tokens for first 12 months; scheduled step-ups at months 7 and 13 based on usage windows.
- Conversion mechanics: client-triggered conversion if two consecutive quarters exceed 85% of committed tokens OR mutual agreement; conversion pricing will be pre-agreed with a floor discount (no more than 10% off list).
- Burst safety net: 1) pre-purchased burst credits included (one-time allocation), 2) SLA-backed on-demand burst lane for critical workloads (response window: 30 minutes, subject to separate SOW appendix).
- True-up & billing: quarterly true-ups with crediting applied to next invoice; invoicing cadence remains quarterly.
- Auto-renew: 60-day notification window; standard opt-out.

Next steps:
- I'll send the amendment + SOW appendix for the SLA-burst lane to Alicia and procurement after the call.
- Alicia / procurement to confirm whether they want 30- or 36-month envelope.
- I'll push the DocuSign flow + HubSpot deal update once we align.

Call confirmed: Wed 2027-05-26 09:00 PST. I'll send calendar invite in a few minutes.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
